prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1116; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a sideswipe while changing lanes and said the other vehicle drifted into their lane on the driver's side. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been cooperative in providing the initial account.

Entry 2: Photos taken at the scene confirm several of the details the claimant described, though no independent witnesses have come forward to speak to how the collision happened. The police report and a witness statement confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 3: Inspection of the vehicle shows damage consistent with the described impact along the driver's side. A few older scratches are visible near the damaged area and may predate this loss; they are being noted separately. Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before the policy coverage began, and the driver is named on the policy.

Entry 4: Claimant reports a wrist fracture from the impact. The injury fits the kind and force of a collision of this type. Medical records show a sensible course of treatment that tapered off as the claimant improved.

Entry 5: Prior records show a minor strain in the same area several years ago, which healed fully with no lasting effects. Claimant was asked about it and acknowledged it, and the current injury is being evaluated on its own findings.

Entry 6: Claimant has added a few small details to the account since the first report, but the core description of the lane change and impact has stayed the same across each interview. The file is being reviewed for settlement based on the medical and vehicle evidence.
